fields.why: The unadjusted models examine race and gender identity as characteristics, and Table 2 reports race-specific ORs vs White with CIs and p-values (Hispanic p=0.043) that the text never discusses: an interpretive-table-only SPD contrast, which the brief caps at, and places at, level 2. B's level 1 treats race only as a covariate/descriptor and gave 2 as its alternative.

Sex as a population bound is defensible because the MSM definition requires reporting being male, but transgender persons are also eligible and the 'male' answer is a gender-identity item, so leaving sex out is also defensible.

verdict: sexual orientation and gender identity: population
sexual orientation and gender identity: stratifier (or covariate)
fields.why: Race and gender identity each get per-level ORs in Table 2 (A: stratifier) and also serve as Table 1 composition and model terms (B: descriptor/covariate); A's roles fit its level-2 reading better, but neither is wrong. The sex entry follows the dimensions verdict.

verdict: sexual orientation and gender identity: behavior
sexual orientation and gender identity: self-identified
fields.why: MSM is defined by self-reported sexual identity or, for straight-identified men, by having sex with men, so behavior and self-identified both fit the population entry. Gender identity is self-identified. Basis is optional, and A's 'sex: self-identified' holds only if sex is recorded at all.

brief_issues: Level 1 vs 2 when an SPD is a model covariate but its per-level ORs are shown in an interpretive table (here from the unadjusted model): the brief has 'race as a confounder is level 1' and also 'interpretive-table-only contrasts are capped at 2'; a rule saying that displayed per-level estimates make it level 2 would settle it.
